Your vehicle may also be searched for forbidden items such as certain types of fresh produce and certain types of meat.

There are several different border posts between SA and Botswana and I can’t remember exactly which ones they used, but in any case, they entered and exited via two different border posts.

Crossing into Botswana everything went smoothly. They had an excellent holiday and saw plenty of wildlife. They started making their way back to SA a few weeks later, which would involve crossing the border again.

They had been tipped off by friends that a bribe would be payable at this particular border post, otherwise the officials would claim that according to their computer, you were driving a stolen vehicle and that it would have to be impounded while they “investigated” the matter. Needless to say, it would be disastrous to be stranded there with your kids.

They waited in the queue of vehicles in sweltering heat with flies buzzing. A fat bantu woman in a uniform came shuffling out from under a tree where she had been napping upright on an unfeasibly tiny wooden stool. There was a blanket on the ground next to the stool, with various items displayed for sale.

Turned out Sisi (a courteous form of address for a woman in the Bantu languages, used disparagingly by White South Africans when referring to a bantu woman) was a Customs officer who was running a private stall on the side during the working hours of her day job.

She lethargically announced that she was going to search the vehicle for forbidden fresh produce – which my relatives had an abundance.

Being well-versed in the ways of Africa, my relative said “Good morning madam. May we browse the fine goods you are selling while you search our vehicle?”

She started rifling through their belongings and came upon numerous forbidden items. “You will buy from my shop?” asked/instructed. To which my relative responded “Well of course my good woman, we’ll take one of these and two of these (utterly useless pieces of crap)”. Money changed hands and she forgot all about the stuff in the vehicle and went back and slowly lowered her tremendous butt onto the tiny wooden stool while swatting away a fly.

Next up, inspection of documents…

A corpulent bantu man looked at the vehicle papers, did some slow motion, one-finger banging on a keyboard and then proclaimed “Our computer says this vehicle is stolen”.

My relative, as cool as a cucumber, produced a wad of cash said “Well sir, with such an outdated computer, it must be very difficult to do your job and it would be remiss of us not to make a donation towards a new computer”.

“Eish, the computer it is very expensive” came the reply.

“Well of course it is sir, please accept our donation towards your expenses”. About two hundred and fifty Rand was handed over – this was in 2014 when it was worth significantly more than it is now (about 15 USD) and they were free to go.

As they moved on, they heard the bantu telling the next hapless driver “Our computer says this vehicle is stolen”.

The end
